alt: The left menu groups the pages by topic.
Open Contact support, then click Send a request to support.
The support form: choose a topic, add a short title and the details.
Settings, Invitations: type the email and click Invite.
The People list. Search by name, then click a person.
A profile has tabs: Personal, Employment, Documents and more.
The Add person form.
The Employment tab, where the manager, team and attendance lead are set.
On the profile, open More actions and choose Archive.
The Onboarding page lists people in onboarding and lets HR start a checklist.
Checklist templates: one default list, and one per position if you want.
The Offboarding page, where you start an offboarding.
Team attendance: who is working now, flags and end-of-day reports.
Hours review: check each week and approve it.
The Corrections tab on the Attendance page.
The Extra hours page, with the requests to review.
The Hours export tab: choose the pay period and download.
The Jibble page shows the connection and the people who are not matched.
The Time off page with its tabs. Approvals holds the requests waiting for you.
The Award tab: choose the person, the days and the reason.
The Schedules page: tick people, then set a schedule.
Import schedules and clients from the attendance sheet.
The Documents page: files that are missing, to verify, or expiring.
Announcements, with the Policies and Pop-up queue tabs.
The Signing page: documents to sign, all documents and templates.
Send a document: choose the file, who signs and the order.
Analytics shows totals only, and hides groups under 5 people.
Assets: the inventory and who has what.
Certificates that expire, with reminders.
Roles and access: choose a person's roles and save.
The support inbox, with the open requests.
Privacy incidents: report one, or handle the ones in the inbox.
Start onboarding: tick the people and choose the start date.
A person's onboarding checklist: who owns each task and what is done.
Start an offboarding: tick the person, then set the last working day and the reason.
An offboarding case: the checklist, and the HR actions such as Remove access now.
The Approvals tab: read the request, then Approve or Decline.
Requests to review: the client, the time window, the reason and the proof.
Open Days to see each day, then click Approve week.
A person's Documents tab: folders, the list of files and the upload buttons.
Upload many files: drag them into the box, then click Upload files.
The New announcement form: title, message and who it is for.
Register an item: tag, name, category and serial number.
The time clock is at the top right of every page.
My time, under Attendance, shows today and your week.
Your clock settings: your time zone and the location option.
Ask for a time correction: choose what happened, say why and add a screenshot.
Report a technical issue: what went wrong, and a screenshot.
Ask to work extra hours: the client, the time, who approved it, and a screenshot.
Time off: your prize days and your requests.
Request time off: leave type, first and last day, and a note.
Your schedule, in your client's time and in Manila time.
My profile: your photo, your details and the request links.
Request a change to your contact details. HR reviews it before it applies.
Your Documents tab: choose the type, add a title and the file, then Upload.
Your onboarding checklist: who owns each task and what is due.
Announcements: the ones that need your acknowledgment are marked.
Read it, then click I have read and understand.
My training: open your assigned course.
My certificates, with the dates they end.
My assets: the equipment assigned to you.
Reviews: your reviews and your goals.
My data: everything ELEVATE holds about you, with downloads and a way to ask HR.
Privacy incidents: click Report an incident.
Say what happened, when, and what you have done. No patient details.
The org chart: the chart view and the list view.
Duplicate people: choose the record that stays, and merge by hand.
Change requests: Pending, Approved and Rejected.
Custom fields: label, key, type, who can see it.
Structure: departments, teams and positions.
Clients: name, time zone, holidays and whether they work with patient information.
Rules, per team: allowed IPs, idle prompt, grace and selfie.
Technical issues: your reports and all reports.
Training status: who passed, who has not, and who is overdue.
Course studio: read, compare and edit the courses.
Reviews: Templates, Launch a cycle and the list of cycles.
Launch a review cycle: name, type, template, who is reviewed and due dates.
Reviews, as a lead: the reviews you write and your team's reviews.
Import from TalentHR: upload, preview, commit, reconcile.
The go-live checklist: some rows check themselves, the rest you tick.
The audit log: who did what, and when.
People records retention: periods, counts and the nightly job.
Safe Voice: say what this is about and what happened. No name is asked.
To read a reply, type your case code and passphrase.
The Applicants page: filters on top, one row for each applicant.
More filters: how it closed, source, tag, keyword match and the talent pool.
Tick applicants, choose what to do, then click Apply.
Possible duplicates: records that look like the same person.
Applicant emails: the built-in wording, and a place to write your own.
The Recruiting page lists your jobs and applicants.
The New job form. A job starts as a draft.
Edit the careers page title, introduction and banner.
Offer templates: the letter and the fields that fill in by themselves.
A job's pipeline: one column for each stage.
Schedule an interview: type, date and time, length, place and interviewers.
On an applicant at the Offer stage, open Make an offer.
Recruiting reports: how far applications got, time in each stage, sources and how applications ended.
The pipeline. Drag a card to another column, or use Move to.
An applicant's page: details, keyword match, talent pool, source and tags, then the resume, notes, interviews and history.
On an applicant's page: where they heard about the job, and their tags.
On the job form: the words to look for in resumes.
An applicant's keyword match: the percentage, the words found and the words missing.
On an applicant's page: the talent pool panel.
